title: Replication lag: measuring it, alerting on it, and the stale read

videos.script: An asynchronous standby is behind. The questions are by how much, and who finds out when it is too much. {{behind}} You measure it two ways: in bytes, as a distance in the log, and in seconds, as the age of what the standby shows. {{measure}} Then a quiet night. One measurement freezes, and the other grows for no reason at all. {{idle}} You pause the standby on purpose, place an order, and look for it there. It is not there. {{stale}} You write the check that tells you, and find that the obvious one passes when the standby is gone. {{alert}} Last, you lose the slot again, as in lesson 11. This time the standby fetches what it missed from the archive, and keeps going. {{archive}}
